This course introduces students to the principles and practice of web
communication and web design, from basic HTML/CSS to JavaScript, responsive layout, and beyond. 
All lecture materials, exercises, and boilerplate code
are published in the course GitHub repository.

## Logistics

Lectures run 14:30--17:30 on Friday and 9:00--11:45 on Saturday. 
All lectures take place in *Laboratorio 2* on the ground floor of the *Passione* building. A low-qual AV broadcast and lecture recording will be available.

## Software Tools

Tools students need installed to follow the course and complete exercises:

- **Web browser** Firefox will be used in class. 

- **Package manager** to quickly install/update software. For Win: install [chocolatey.org](https://chocolatey.org/); For Mac: install [brew.sh](https://brew.sh/).

- **Code editor** [code.visualstudio.com/](https://code.visualstudio.com/); also available online at [vscode.dev/](https://vscode.dev/)
- **document converter** from [pandoc.org/](https://pandoc.org/), used under the hood by Quarto; also available online at [pandoc.org/try/](https://pandoc.org/try/)
- **Renderer** [quarto.org/](https://quarto.org/) for authoring and rendering course materials (HTML, PDF, RevealJS slides)
- **Version control software** [git-scm.com/](https://git-scm.com/), and a [github.com/](https://github.com/) account — for cloning the course repository and publishing work
- **A modern Git manager**, e.g. [fork.dev](https://fork.dev/)

## Exams

Prepare a Web Communication project consisting of a *pitch deck* for a technical audience, a stub web page with styles, AV contents, links etc parked on your GitHub account and coordinated with email campaign plans and social media presence (IG, FB, X, WA etc.). 
The oral exam consists of presenting your project and showing *ownership* of the code.

**Exam dates** December 18 and 19 in person at the *sala seminari* on the second floor of the *Passione* building (TBC). Arrangements are available for Erasmus/exchange students who need to leave Milan earlier.
For 2027, January 13 and 14 (TBC) and dates in March and July.
